existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `DetectedIssue` has material local breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. Top concerns: `status` required-value-set change, `patient` to `subject`, `severity` primitive-to-CodeableConcept, and the `code`/`category` semantic split. Main uncertainty is terminology detail, especially v3 ActCode expansions and the R6 `processing-error` status inconsistency.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be field-aware rather than purely syntactic. Patient references can usually be renamed to subject, severity codes must be wrapped as CodeableConcepts, and status values require clinical policy mapping. Code/category migration needs terminology and implementation review because validation may not catch semantic drift. Downgrade from R6 to R4 is lossy for non-Patient subjects, new author targets, `identifiedTiming`, and R6-only context/management fields.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for some terminology and semantic conclusions because no official diff, full terminology expansions, or narrative ballot notes were supplied. The computable R6 DetectedIssueStatus value set and R6 status text disagree about `processing-error`, so that part needs specification review.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
DetectedIssue keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 3 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 1 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 1, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 28/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

1 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: DetectedIssue.status required binding changed from ObservationStatus to DetectedIssueStatus and removes several R4 status codes
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-valid status codes removed from the required R6 value set fail validation; there is also runtime/API/codegen enum churn and R6-to-R4 loss for mitigated.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: DetectedIssue.patient was replaced by DetectedIssue.subject and subject target types were broadened
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with patient contain an unknown R6 element and generated models/FHIRPath expressions must switch to subject; R6 non-Patient subjects are R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: DetectedIssue.severity changed from required-bound primitive code to preferred-bound CodeableConcept
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: populated R4 severity strings are the wrong JSON shape for R6; runtime/API/codegen types change from scalar or enum-like code to CodeableConcept, with R6-to-R4 loss for non-legacy codings.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: DetectedIssue.code no longer carries the high-level category; R6 adds category for categorization and changes the code binding
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the same R6 `code` element can accept old-looking CodeableConcepts while changing their intended meaning; there is also runtime/API/search/index behavior risk and R6-to-R4 loss for separate multiple categories.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: DetectedIssue.author can now be Patient or RelatedPerson as well as practitioner/device actors
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: Patient and RelatedPerson authors cannot be represented in the base R4 author target list, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
